title: The Power of Self-Control: Escaping the Mire of Mediocrity
summary: Addressing the universal struggles with weakness and poor choices, President Hughes delivers a compelling discourse on self-control and self-discipline as the keys to expanding personal agency. He warns against a global economy built on consumer addiction—specifically targeting fast food, video games, and mindless internet browsing—and shares a personal account of firing a top executive due to gaming addiction. He outlines transformative daily habits, such as exercising 150 minutes a week, reading two hours a day, and writing 500 words a day, concluding with an extensive collection of classic quotes on self-mastery from world thinkers and his personal hero, Theodore Roosevelt.
